tion to a close, Mr. Paxton moved his family to a new home in the new territory, as he had been a leading part in developing West Texas, settling near Anson in Jones County, where he bought land in cultivation, became a fine stock breeder, and acquired fine stock and fine stock.

Soon after 1900, Mr. Paxton's children having married or gone forth from the old home to build their careers, he made his home with a daughter in Tulsa, Texas, and later in Haskell and Haskell, Texas. He was always a student of the history of the frontier days and acquired quite a nice library. Mr. Paxton died April 10, 1914, at the age of nearly 81 years.

He was always a student interested in education, joined the ministry of his family's church the Christian Church early in his life. In his later years he was an active observer of and participated in the life about him, spending time in public life. He gave pot[?] a just and earnest worker and only active member with the Christian church and was fond and loved by all.

ROBERT ROBERSON HALSELL

A complete biography of the life and works of Robert Roberson Halsell is badly needed as a pioneer in education in Texas, and it is hoped that some day such a biography may be written. For the present the outline of his life sketch are here reproduced in photostat as a memorial to the college. The sketch was written by a former student, Professor N. W. Verina, of the University of Texas, Mrs. Welborn of Paris, Texas, and Mr. Anderson himself.

Robert Roberson Halsell was born in Adair County, Kentucky, November 20, 1833, and died in 1920. His parents were William and Mary (Halsell) Halsell. Thomas J. Chenoweth, Jr., of Sherman, Texas. Nineteen grandchildren and six great-grandchildren.
